gravitee/api-definition.json.superseded_because: Its upstream target https://<DATABRICKS_HOST>/api/2.0/delta-sharing is wrong twice: wrong HOST (the workspace host is not the sharing host) and wrong PATH (no issued credential contains /api/2.0/delta-sharing; the real path is /api/2.0/opensharing/metastores/<id>). This is the better explanation for T-01 never having produced a read through the gateway.
gravitee/api-definition.json.what_it_still_contributes: Its policy identifiers and configuration field names were verified against this installation's own plugins/policies schema endpoints. That verification is carried into policy-classes.yaml, which is why the file is superseded rather than discarded.
gravitee/api-definition.json.retire_in_gravitee_by: RETRACTED 2026-10-21, before anyone acted on it. The live API at /opensharing-demo/ must be stopped, its plans closed, and the API DELETED BEFORE the family is imported.
gravitee/api-definition.json.retire_in_gravitee_by_superseded_text: The two live APIs (/opensharing-demo/ and /delta-sharing/) must be stopped and deleted AFTER the family imports and T-01 passes, not before -- deleting the old route first removes the only working comparison.
gravitee/api-definition.json.retire_in_gravitee_by_retracted_because: Three observations, each sufficient on its own. (1) SEQUENCING: a Gravitee context path is a PREFIX, so the existing API at /opensharing-demo/ COLLIDES with every /opensharing-demo/<slug> listener in this family. The old API does not merely survive the import -- it BLOCKS it. On the 2026-10-21 run only the F1 storage proxy imported, because /storage-proxy/ was the one path with no collision. (2) The 'only working comparison' did not exist. That API has flows: 0 -- no perimeter policies at all -- and its upstream is pinned to the sharing host of a credential that EXPIRED 2026-10-18, so it cannot produce a successful read for any recipient and never could. It has been an unpoliced pass-through to a dead host. (3) Worse than useless: because it prefix-matches, it ANSWERED this family's paths by forwarding them upstream with the recipient slug glued into the protocol path, producing Databricks 404s that read like gateway refusals. That is B-44, and this sentence is what kept the blocking object alive long enough to cause it.
gravitee/api-definition.json.retraction_note: Carried in place rather than edited away (B-19). The wrong advice was mine, it was specific, and it was the kind that gets followed.
